description:
A Lawful Development Certificate should be granted because the proposed works at 23 Greenfield Drive, London N2 9AF are lawful and do not require express planning permission.
The property is an existing, long-established single-family dwellinghouse in Class C3 use. The proposed development, as shown on drawings A100 (Proposed Plan) and A101 (Existing Plan), consists of:

A modest extension to the ground floor front entrance/front door area, which falls within the permitted development rights under Class D (Porches) of Part 1, Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) and meets the relevant limitations of that Class.
Internal reconfiguration of walls and rooms (including relocation of the WC and adjustments to the kitchen, dining, living, study, and bedroom layouts), which are internal works that do not affect the external appearance of the building and therefore do not constitute “development” under Section 55(2)(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
Installation of a single rooflight on the rear roof slope, which is permitted under Class B of Part 1, Schedule 2 of the GPDO 2015. The rooflight has been designed not to protrude more than 150 mm beyond the plane of the original roof slope, as noted on drawing A100.

The site is not located within a Conservation Area, and there is no Article 4 Direction in the London Borough of Haringey that removes or restricts the relevant permitted development rights (Class B or Class D) for this proposal. The standard national permitted development provisions therefore apply in full.
For these reasons, the proposed development is lawful and a Certificate of Lawfulness of Proposed Development should be granted.
